transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what brought me in is that my head just feels really foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things that I shouldn't be. Like... I'll get my appointment times wrong, or mix up the dates for exhibits, or I can't remember which volunteer I've already called on the phone. It's just very frustrating, so I thought I needed to come in.
How long have you been noticing this foggy feeling and trouble remembering things—days, weeks, or longer?

Well, I'd say it's been going on for about four months now. It seemed to start right around the time we had some water damage that... well, it pushed us into doing a remodel. So, yes, about four months of this.
Since this began around the time of the water damage and remodel, have you also been feeling unusually sad, down, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, actually. I just don't have the energy for much of anything anymore. Things I used to love, like my watercolors, my tomato plants, line dancing, and watching the cardinals out back, just sit there now and I can't make myself care about them.
How has your sleep been over these past four months—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

My sleep? Well, I haven't really noticed any big changes there. I mean, I go to bed around the same time I always do, and I seem to be sleeping about the same amount. I'm not tossing and turning all night or anything, and I'm not sleeping the day away either. It's just... normal, I guess.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like feeling unusually cold, gaining weight, having dry skin, or constipation?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My weight has stayed about the same, and I don't feel any colder than usual. No dry skin or stomach issues either. Just the lack of energy and the foggy feeling, really.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or down on yourself these past four months?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel guilty about anything, and I don't feel worthless. It's really just the lack of energy and not caring about my hobbies like I used to. But I don't feel bad about myself, if that makes sense.

Do you find yourself feeling anxious, overwhelmed, or preoccupied specifically about the water damage and remodel, or does the low mood and fogginess feel present all the time regardless of what's happening with the house?

Well, it's not really about the house. I mean, the remodel is a nuisance, sure, but I don't feel anxious or worried about it. The fogginess and the low energy... they're just there all the time. It doesn't seem to matter what I'm doing or what's going on with the water damage. It's just this constant heavy feeling, no matter what.

When you mix up appointment times or forget who you've called, does it feel like you truly can't recall the information afterward, or more like you have trouble focusing long enough to take it in in the first place?

I think it's more that my head just feels foggy. That's really what brought me in, actually. I just keep mixing up simple things. Like... I'll get appointment times wrong, or I'll mess up the dates for the art exhibits, or I'll forget which volunteer I already called. It's not that I wasn't paying attention, it's just like the information gets all jumbled up in my head because of this fog.
Thinking back over these four months, did the foggy, forgetful feeling start before the low mood and loss of interest in your hobbies, or did they both begin around the same time?

I'm really not sure which came first. It seems like they both just sort of crept up on me around the same time. I didn't notice the fogginess before the low energy or anything like that... it feels like it all just kind of rolled in together over these last few months.
In the past four months, have you started any new medications or supplements, had any illnesses, infections, or a head injury, or increased your use of alcohol or other substances?

No, nothing like that. I haven't started taking anything new, no new pills or vitamins. I haven't been sick, and I definitely haven't hit my head. And I don't really drink much anyway, so that hasn't changed either. Everything's just been exactly the same, except for this... this fog.

Are there times when you feel a bit more like your usual self, even briefly, and if so, does the fogginess and forgetfulness improve during those moments, or does it stay just as bad no matter how you're feeling emotionally?

I don't really have moments where I feel like my usual self lately. It's just been this same low, foggy feeling the whole time. I haven't noticed any times where the fog lifts or my mood gets better, even for a little while. It's just been a steady... I guess a steady decline for the past four months.
Have you or any close family members ever been diagnosed with a thyroid problem, or has anyone mentioned noticing a swelling or lump in your neck?

No, I don't think so. I haven't had any thyroid issues, and as far as I know, nobody in my family has either. And no one's ever said anything about a lump or swelling in my neck. I haven't noticed anything like that myself, anyway.

If I asked you to remember a short list of words or do a simple calculation right now, do you think you'd struggle with that, or is it really just the day-to-day memory for appointments and details that's affected?

Well, I think I'd probably struggle with the words or the math right now, too, to be honest. My head just feels so foggy. That's really what brought me in to see you in the first place. I just keep mixing up simple things... mostly those day-to-day details you mentioned. Like my appointment times, or the exhibit dates, or even trying to remember which volunteer I already called. I just can't seem to keep any of it straight.
I'm going to say three words—apple, table, and penny—and I'd like you to repeat them back to me now, and then again in a few minutes. Can you do that for me?
Apple, table, penny. I can do that now, but... well, we'll see if I can remember them in a few minutes. Like I said, my memory just hasn't been great lately.
Now, can you tell me the three words I asked you to remember earlier?

Oh, dear. Um... let me think. 

No, I'm sorry, my mind is just completely blank. I can't remember any of them. Like I said, it's just... it's all so foggy up there right now. I knew I'd probably forget.
Let's try again with a hint: one of the words was a fruit, one was a piece of furniture, and one was a type of coin. With those hints, can you recall any of the three words now?

A fruit... maybe an apple? And a piece of furniture... a chair? A coin, um, a dime? 

I'm sorry, I'm really just guessing at this point. Even with you giving me those hints, the exact words you said just aren't coming back to me.
Can you tell me today's date, and where we are right now?

Today's date? Let's see... I think it's Tuesday, maybe the 14th? Or the 15th. I'm honestly not entirely sure of the exact date right now. 

As for where we are, we're at the clinic. Your office. That much I do know.

Has this fogginess affected your ability to manage everyday tasks on your own—like paying bills, cooking, driving, or keeping up with your usual responsibilities—or are you still managing those independently?

Well, yes, it really has. I'm not managing things on my own very well right now. 

I’ve actually missed some doctor visits recently, and... well, I tangled up my schedule for the senior center so badly that my husband has had to step in and take over. He's been helping me with making phone calls and keeping the calendar straight. Even things like making decisions on house repairs—I always used to handle those myself without any trouble, but he has to help me with them now because I just can't seem to keep it all straight.
Since this fogginess began about four months ago, would you say it has been steadily getting worse and worse each month, or has it stayed about the same level of severity since it first started?

I... I really couldn't say for sure. It's hard to measure something like that when you're in the middle of it. 

I don't know if it's steadily getting worse, or if it's just been the same level of bad since it all started. I just know it's been there, but I haven't really noticed a clear difference from one month to the next.

When you were trying to recall those three words, did it feel like you were genuinely trying your best but the information just wasn't there, or did you find it hard to even motivate yourself to try to remember?
I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I tried, but... I don't know if it was a lack of motivation or if the words just wouldn't come. I just couldn't pull them up.
